# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 4 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_004_page_001.jpg

---

4:1 Better is childlessness with virtue; for there is immortality in the memory of virtue, since it is acknowledged by God and by men.

4:2 While virtue is present, people imitate it; and when it has departed, they long for it; and crowned in triumph throughout all ages, it wins the prize in the contest for what is undefiled.

4:3 But the prolific offspring of the ungodly will be of no benefit, and none of their illegitimate shoots will strike deep root or take firm hold.

4:4 For even if they flourish for a time, they will be shaken by the wind, and being rooted in nothing, will be torn up by its force.

4:5 Their branches will snap before they reach maturity, and their fruit will be useless — too unripe to eat and fit for nothing.

4:6 For children born of unlawful unions are witnesses of evil against their parents when they are called to account.

4:7 But the righteous man, even if he dies early, will be at rest.

4:8 For honorable old age is not a matter of length of time, nor is it measured by number of years;

4:9 rather, understanding is the grey hair of man, and a blameless life is the measure of a ripe old age.

4:10 There was one who pleased God and was loved by him, and while living among sinners he was translated.

4:11 He was snatched away lest wickedness pervert his understanding, or treachery deceive his soul.

4:12 For the bewitchment of trivial things obscures what is truly good, and the wandering of desire subverts an innocent mind.

4:13 Having been made perfect in a short time, he fulfilled the span of long years;

4:14 for his soul was pleasing to the Lord, therefore the Lord took him quickly out from the midst of wickedness.

4:15 Yet the peoples see this and do not understand, nor do they take to heart that grace and mercy are with God's chosen, and that he watches over his holy ones.

4:16 The righteous man who has died will condemn the ungodly who are still living, and a youth whose life was completed early will condemn the prolonged old age of the unrighteous.

4:17 For they will see the end of the wise man, and will not understand what the Lord had purposed for him or why he kept him safe.

4:18 They will look on and despise him, but the Lord will laugh at them.

4:19 After this they will themselves become a dishonored corpse and an object of contempt among the dead forever; for the Lord will dash them down speechless and shattered, and will uproot them from their foundations; they will be left utterly desolate and in anguish, and their memory will perish.

4:20 They will come with terror to the reckoning of their sins, and their lawless deeds will confront them to their face.

---

*LOGOS notes: "Translated" at v. 10 is the classical theological term for Enoch's assumption — metetethe (LXX Gen 5:24). "Bewitchment" renders goēteia precisely; this is the author's deliberately disturbing metaphor — wickedness as sorcery. Verse 13's "made perfect" (teleiōtheis) is preserved; the completion/perfection concept is integral to the argument that early death is not failure but fulfillment.*
